region.text: Mers-el-Kebir (Mazalquivir) on the coast west of Oran

ledger.note: 1505: Spain captures Mers-el-Kebir, the first foothold. 'In 1505, the Spanish captured the city of Mers-El-Kebir'; the enclaves list has Mers el-Kebir 1505-1708 and 1732-1792.

18 May 1509: Pedro Navarro storms Oran for Cardinal Cisneros. The Christians stormed the city 'on 18 May'; 'On 20 May, Cisneros entered the city, already conquered'; Oran 'was controlled by the Kingdom of Tlemcen'.

1 November 1707: the Algerians besiege Oran. 'On November 1, 1707, Ouzoum Hassan, a commander from Algiers sent his army to take the fort of Saint-Philippe', which officially started the siege (War of the Spanish Succession).
20 January 1708: Oran falls to the Bey of Mascara. 'The Bey took control of Oran on January 20, 1708... after 400 Spanish soldiers surrendered'.
4 April 1708: Mers el-Kebir falls and the siege ends. 'the Algerians captured the city on April 4' (infobox: siege ended 4 April 1708), with 2,000 captives.
4 April 1708: Spain loses Mers-el-Kebir, its last foothold. The Algerians took Mers el-Kebir on 4 April, after 2,000 captives; 'ruled and administered by Algiers from 1708' (1732 page).

1 July 1732: Spain retakes Oran. The garrison abandoned the city and the Spanish 'entered the city without any trouble' after the news was confirmed on 1 July 1732; 'The next day, 2 July, the city of Mers el-Kebir also capitulated'; led by José Carrillo de Albornoz, Duke of Montemar, who left 6,000 men.
1790: the Algerians besiege Oran again after an earthquake. 'Forces of the Deylik of Algeria under Mohammed el-Kebir besieged the city again, taking advantage of an earthquake' (the 1790 earthquake).
1792: the Spanish troops retreat. 'In 1792 the Spanish troops retreated, ending Spanish rule'; the enclaves list has Oran evacuated in early 1792.
1792: Spain gives up Oran and Mers el-Kebir. 'Algerian reconquest: 1792' (infobox); 'The town stayed under Ottoman control until 1831, when the Kingdom of France conquered it'.

wars.name: Spanish conquest of Oran
wars.outcome: Pedro Navarro, on behalf of Cardinal Cisneros, stormed Oran on 18 May 1509; Cisneros entered on 20 May. Mers-el-Kebir had been taken in 1505.

wars.name: Siege of Oran (1707-1708)
wars.outcome: Siege from 1 November 1707; Oran fell on 20 January 1708 and Mers el-Kebir on 4 April 1708 to Bey Mustapha Bouchelaghem during the War of the Spanish Succession.

wars.name: Spanish conquest of Oran (1732)
wars.outcome: The Duke of Montemar's expedition retook Oran on 1 July and Mers el-Kebir on 2 July 1732 without a fight; Bouchelaghem later tried repeatedly to retake the city.

wars.name: Siege of Oran (1790-1792)
wars.outcome: After an earthquake the Algerians under Mohammed el-Kebir besieged Oran; in 1792 the Spanish retreated, ending Spanish rule.
wars.note: The page gives years only; the sibling Regency of Algiers dossier carries the treaty dates.

certainty.note: Two fortress-cities: the walls are the territory; the 25 km circle is the grid's minimum around a coastal town, not a frontier.

notes: Cliopatria has no Spanish Oran row (the Spanish Empire row's shape does not distinguish it). Start 1505 (Mers-el-Kebir) rather than the infobox's 1509 (Oran) because the two fortress-cities were held, lost and retaken together; the infobox lists 1509, 1708, 1732 and 1792 as its dates. Months: 18 May 1509 (storming), 20 January 1708 (Oran), 4 April 1708 (Mers el-Kebir), 1 and 2 July 1732 (Oran, Mers el-Kebir). The 1792 withdrawal has no month on the pages opened (the sibling Regency dossier has the 1791 agreements and the evacuation). The enclaves list gives 1791 for Oran's end and 1792 for Mers el-Kebir; the Spanish Oran page gives 1792. The sibling dossiers record the same events against 'crown-of-castile' (zayyanid losses 1505, 1509) and 'spanish-empire' (regency-of-algiers 1708, 1732, 1790-1792); this dossier's slug spanish-oran is the colony-level counterpart, and the integrator may map the Spanish Empire strings onto it. Other Spanish presidios (Bougie 1510-1555, Tripoli 1510-1530, the Algiers peñon 1510-1529, Melilla 1497-, Peñon de Velez, Alhucemas, Larache 1610-1689, La Mamora 1614-1681, Asilah, Santa Cruz de la Mar Pequena, Honaine, Annaba, Bizerte, La Goulette, Tunis, Sousse, Monastir, Mahdia, Djerba) are on the enclaves list and not in this dossier.
